name: sol_token_nfe1_2
description: Reentrancy via ERC721/1155 receiver hooks during token minting or transfer
question: The source file in `source` implements an ERC721 or ERC1155 token (or calls into one) that invokes the receiver hook (onERC721Received or onERC1155Received) via safeMint/safeTransfer or equivalent, and performs critical state updates (such as balance, supply, ownership, or accounting changes) after the external receiver callback, or otherwise lacks a reentrancy guard or checks-effects-interactions ordering around the hook, allowing a malicious receiver contract to reenter and exploit inconsistent state. This excludes cases where all state is finalized before the hook call, where a reentrancy guard protects the function, or where the hook target is guaranteed trusted/non-contract.
criteria: mint() calls _safeMint which invokes onERC721Received before totalSupply or balances are updated, allowing reentrant minting
withdrawal or claim function calls safeTransferFrom (ERC721/1155) to an arbitrary receiver before marking the claim/withdrawal as completed
batch transfer function loops over token IDs and updates ownership mappings only after triggering onERC1155BatchReceived callback
public mint function has no nonReentrant modifier despite calling _safeMint that triggers external receiver hook
sale/auction contract sends NFT via safeTransferFrom before deleting the listing or updating price state, enabling reentrant re-purchase
